recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. If the work group later wants normative duplicate-handling rules for multiple ImagingStudy resources with the same Study Instance UID, handle that as a new ImagingStudy policy or implementation guide decision rather than as a FHIR-35994 carry-forward edit.
issue_request: FHIR-35994 was a Published/Persuasive R5 Imaging Integration clarification request asking the ImagingStudy page to explain how to handle multiple ImagingStudy resources that reference the same DICOM Study or different subsets, and whether ImagingSelection should be used for subsets.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied through the June 2022 Imaging changes. Jira comments point to merge commit c138fb1b9ed930251866ab1da3be7d524b3fb1d4, which updated ImagingStudy Boundaries and Relationships to describe ImagingStudy as storing details of an entire DICOM Study and added ImagingSelection as the resource for a specific set of DICOM images, frames, or other DICOM instances.
additional_context: Later Applied issues revisited the same overlap. FHIR-47275 explicitly removed the old wording that an ImagingStudy may reference a subset and that multiple ImagingStudy resources may reference the same DICOM Study, while noting in Jira comments that base FHIR is generally silent on duplicate resources sharing a business identifier such as DICOM Study Instance UID. FHIR-50769, FHIR-54814, and FHIR-54797 refined the current ImagingStudy/ImagingSelection wording.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active current source already says one ImagingStudy resource SHALL reference one DICOM Study, ImagingStudy stores details of an entire DICOM Study, and ImagingSelection references a subset of a DICOM Study. Restoring the old duplicate/subset sentence would conflict with later Applied R6 decisions.
